tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which localization projects they have in MultiLocale. Returns each project's id, name, default locale, languages and timestamps, up to 100 projects. Not for listing the strings inside a project.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Use this when someone asks about one localization project, such as which languages it has or its default locale. Returns the project's id, name, default locale, configured locales and creation and edit times. Not for how complete its translations are.

tools.name: add_project
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to create a new localization project with a given name and languages. Returns the new project with its default locale and locales; if the name is taken it returns already-exists and creates nothing. Not for adding a language to an existing project.

tools.name: update_project
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to change a project's default locale, replace its list of languages, or set its translation context. Returns which fields changed. The language list is replaced as a whole, no strings are translated or deleted, and the project name stays fixed. Not for adding a language wi

tools.name: list_phrases
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to see the translation strings in a project, optionally in one language or for one key. Returns up to 100 phrases with id, key, language and value, plus the total count. Not for finding strings by the words they contain.

tools.name: get_phrase
tools.description: Use this when someone asks how one exact key is translated, in every language or in one. Returns that key's text per locale, up to 24 locales and 2,000 characters each, with machine-translation flags and the projects sharing it, and renders a phrase card. Not for searching keys by text.

tools.name: search_phrases
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to find translation strings that contain a word or phrase, in their keys or text. Returns up to 100 matches with id, key, language and value from a case-insensitive match within one project. Not for one exact key.

tools.name: find_duplicate_phrase_values
tools.description: Use this when someone wants to clean up a project by finding keys that repeat the same default-language text. Returns up to 25 repeated values with the keys that share them, scanning 1,000 default-locale strings by default and at most 2,000. Not for untranslated strings.

tools.name: find_missing_translations
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which strings are not translated yet, or how complete each language is. Returns completion percentages and up to 25 missing keys per locale, for one locale or up to 10, compared with the default locale. Nothing is translated or written. Not for filling in the missing trans

tools.name: export_locale_dictionary
tools.description: Use this when someone wants the key and value pairs of one language, for example to review or copy a translation file. Returns up to 50 entries per call (25 by default) sorted by key, values cut to 500 characters, with nextSkip for the next page. Not for a complete file download, which the MultiLoca

tools.name: list_team_members
tools.description: Use this when someone asks who is on their MultiLocale team or what role each person has. Returns each member's display name and role, up to 100 members (no emails, ids or contact details). Not for inviting or removing people.

tools.name: add_phrase
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to add a new string or key to their app's translations. Returns the created key with one machine translation per configured locale, made from the source text in the default locale. A key that already exists returns already-exists and is left unchanged. Not for changing an

tools.name: update_phrase
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to fix or change the text of one key in one language. Returns the previous and new text and the projects sharing that string; the change applies in all of them and marks the text as human-edited. Not for adding a new key.

tools.name: add_locale
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to add a new language to a project and translate their strings into it. Returns the updated language list and how many strings were machine-translated, one per key, all before anything is saved, so a very large project can time out. Not for a language the project already h

tools.name: share_phrase
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to reuse a key's translations in other projects, such as a common button label. Returns the target projects and how many language rows were attached, up to 25 targets; later edits to that string apply in every attached project. Not for a copy that can differ per project.

tools.name: delete_phrase
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to remove a key from their translations. Returns how many language rows were deleted and which other projects shared them; a shared string is deleted permanently for those projects too. Not for removing only one language's translation.

tools.name: open_multilocale
tools.description: Use this when someone wants to open Multilocale and browse their workspace interactively. Localization projects, strings and translations. Starts with up to 100 items. Not for changing data.

tools.name: show_project_overview
tools.description: Use this when someone wants a quick overview of one of their localization projects. Returns an overview card with the project's default locale, up to 24 configured locales and timestamps. Not for translation completeness.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "update_project" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "add_locale" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_team_members · Private data: export_locale_dictionary, list_team_members · Public sink: find_duplicate_phrase_values, share_phrase · Destructive: delete_phrase.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_team_members · Private data: export_locale_dictionary, list_team_members · Public sink: find_duplicate_phrase_values, share_phrase · Destructive: delete_phrase

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
